title: 2016 AMC 10A 22
statement: For some positive integer \(n,\) the number \(110n^3\) has \(110\) positive integer divisors, including \(1\) and the number \(110n^3.\) How many positive integer divisors does the number \(81n^4\) have?

solutions.text:
The prime factorization is \(110=2\cdot5\cdot11\). If \(110n^3\) has \(110=2\cdot5\cdot11\) divisors, then it has exactly three prime factors, with exponents \(1,4,10\) in some order.

For each of the primes \(2,5,11\), its exponent in \(110n^3\) is \(1\) more than a multiple of \(3\). The exponents \(1,4,10\) all have this form, so the corresponding exponents in \(n\) are \(0,1,3\) in some order.

In \(81n^4=3^4n^4\), the exponents from \(n^4\) are therefore \(0,4,12\), in some order, along with the exponent \(4\) on prime \(3\). Hence the divisor count is \[ \begin{aligned} &(0+1)\cdot(4+1)\cdot(12+1) \\ &\quad {}\cdot(4+1)=325. \end{aligned} \]

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Those exponents are all \(1\pmod3\), so they can come from \(110n^3\)
